CitationRead.description:
A source an answer cites. ``source_id`` matches the ``[S1]`` or ``[D1]``
markers in the message content; ``ordinal`` numbers the rendered source list.

``kind`` says which: a web page (``url`` and ``display_url`` set) or a
chunk of one of the user's documents (``document_id`` and ``page`` set,
``title`` is the filename, no URL).
CitationRead.title: CitationRead

ConversationCreate.description: A new thread. The title is optional — most clients let it be derived.
ConversationCreate.title: ConversationCreate

ConversationDetail.description:
A single conversation, with what a freshly loaded page needs to resume.

``active_run_id`` is set while a run is queued or running. A browser that
reloads mid-answer has lost its stream; this is how it learns there is a
run to recover through ``GET /runs/{id}``, from any tab or device.
ConversationDetail.title: ConversationDetail

DocumentList.description: Every document in the conversation, in upload order. Capped, so unpaginated.
DocumentList.title: DocumentList

error_code.description: Set when status is failed, e.g. embedding_unavailable.
error_code.title: Error Code

status.description: processing: stored and being prepared; ready: answers can use it; failed: it could not be prepared (see error_code). Poll while processing.

DocumentsRetrievedEvent.description:
Which of the conversation's documents the answer draws on (ADR-0015).

Names and counts only, never document text: the passages reach the user
as citations, and only the ones the answer actually cites.
DocumentsRetrievedEvent.title: DocumentsRetrievedEvent

details.description: Optional structured context, e.g. failing fields.
details.title: Details

message.description: Human-readable summary. May be reworded; do not parse.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Correlates with the X-Request-ID response header.
request_id.title: Request Id

LivenessResponse.description: Process is up. Deliberately independent of every external dependency.
LivenessResponse.title: LivenessResponse

MessageCompletedEvent.description:
Terminal. ``message`` is canonical: clients replace the streamed text
with its content rather than trusting their own concatenation.
MessageCompletedEvent.title: MessageCompletedEvent

MessageResponse.description:
Deliberately uninformative acknowledgement.

Used where a precise answer would disclose whether an account exists.
MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse

ReadinessResponse.description: Process can serve traffic: required dependencies answered.

checks.description: Per-dependency result, keyed by dependency name.
checks.title: Checks

ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

RunCreate.description:
Start a run: either for a new message, or to retry the latest one.

A retry reuses the user message already stored, so trying again after a
failure or a stop never duplicates the question in the history.
RunCreate.title: RunCreate

RunRead.description: A run's canonical state — the recovery path after a lost stream.
RunRead.title: RunRead

SourceRead.description:
Metadata of a search result. Deliberately no snippet: progress events
describe what was found, they do not carry retrieved page text.
SourceRead.title: SourceRead

TokenResponse.description:
The access token only.

The refresh token is never in a response body — it goes out as an
HttpOnly cookie so that script running in the page cannot read it.
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

UserRead.description: What the API exposes about an account. No password hash, ever.
UserRead.title: UserRead

post.description:
Always returns the same acknowledgement.

A different status, body, or timing for a known versus unknown address
would turn this endpoint into an account-enumeration oracle.

post.description:
Upload a PDF. Returns at once with status ``processing``; poll until ``ready``.

The body is read here, after authentication, the rate limit, and the
ownership check have all passed. Declaring the file as a parameter would
have FastAPI read and spool the whole body first, so an anonymous or
throttled caller could still make the server receive 10 MB.

file.description: The PDF. At most MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (10 MiB by default).
